html:
The Zacateco were a people of the dry plateau of north central Mexico, in today's state of Zacatecas and northeastern Durango. They were one of the many northern peoples the Nahua lumped together as Chichimeca.

They lived in small mobile bands, hunting, gathering mesquite pods and cactus fruit, and farming a little. In 1546 Spaniards found rich silver at Zacatecas, in the middle of their country, and a road of mines and forts soon ran north from Mexico City. The Zacateco, with the Guachichil, the Caxcan and others, fought back in the long Chichimeca War of about 1550 to 1590. Peace came through gifts of food and cloth and the settling of Christian Indian farmers from the south among them. Afterward the Zacateco were absorbed into the mining towns and ranches of New Spain, though families in Zacatecas and Durango still claim descent from them. The map's Zacatecs territory shows them in later centuries.
